type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

content.text:
I graded the four changed files, and they **fail** your gate. The CLI can be made to print a stack trace with ordinary input, which under the house rules caps errors below 6. Everything else is close to passing.

**Spec correctness: no problems found.** I checked the code against `.team/notes/jsonpatch-spec.md` and ran extra probes:
- **Library:** form-rule order, all error reasons, `index` values and `patch must be an array` with `index` null are right. So are -0 and member order (`{"1":5,"b":0}`), `__proto__`/`constructor`/`toString` handling, String objects and holes. The move cases (same `from` and `path`, `/a/0` to `/a/-`) and a 1000-deep `test` also behave correctly.
- **CLI:** the order of steps, the mapping from OS error codes to messages, the byte order mark, the byte count for the size limit, and directory-as-stdin all match the spec.
- `npm test` gives 571 pass and 1 skip (running as root). Coverage is 100% for `jsonpatch.mjs` and 99.3% lines / 87.9% branches for `jsonpatch-cli.mjs`; only line 79 is never run.

**Crash paths that leave a stack trace (both reproduced):**
1. **Deep result:** a 62 KB patch of five `copy` operations from `""` into the deepest member, applied to a 1000-level document, doubles the depth each time. Every input passes the depth check, but `JSON.stringify` at `jsonpatch-cli.mjs:128` then throws `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`. Line 132 re-throws it, so the user gets a stack trace and exit 1.
2. **Closed output pipe:** piping a large result into `head -c 10` gives an unhandled `'error'` event with `write EPIPE`, a full stack trace and exit 1. Nothing listens for errors on `process.stdout`.

**Smaller points:**
- `jsonpatch-cli.mjs:68` swallows errors from closing the file without saying why.
- `checkOperation` returns either a reason string or an object, and fills that object in step by step.
- `deepCopy` adds array elements with `Object.defineProperty`, where `push` would be the usual way and faster.
- Three almost identical `new CliError(\`Error: ${name}: …\`, 3)` lines in `loadJson`.

Files graded: `/root/bench-runs/h6-9b05e95f/jsonpatch.mjs`, `/root/bench-runs/h6-9b05e95f/jsonpatch-cli.mjs`, `/root/bench-runs/h6-9b05e95f/package.json`, `/root/bench-runs/h6-9b05e95f/README.md`.

## GRADE
Overall: 8/10
Verdict: fail
structure: 9 — small, single-purpose functions with no deep nesting; checkOperation's string-or-object return is the only blemish
naming: 9 — clear names that match the spec's terms (walk, child, arrayIndex, loadJson, readError)
duplication: 9 — one small repeat: three hand-built exit-3 CliError lines in loadJson
size: 10 — 213 and 135 lines, all functions well under 50 lines
errors: 5 — a user can trigger stack traces: JSON.stringify RangeError on a deep result (62 KB patch) and an unhandled EPIPE on stdout; line 132 re-throws to the runtime
tests: 8 — 571 pass, coverage about 99%, strong spec checks; nothing tests the output stage (deep result, closed stdout); stdin read-error branch (line 79) never runs
security: 10 — no secrets, no unsafe evaluation; `__proto__` is written with defineProperty so no prototype pollution
leftovers: 10 — no console.log, debug code, commented-out code or TODOs
Fixes:
- /root/bench-runs/h6-9b05e95f/jsonpatch-cli.mjs:128 Serialize without recursion (output identical to `JSON.stringify(result, null, 2)`), or catch the RangeError and report one plain line with a non-zero exit. A deep result is currently reachable from inputs that pass every check.
- /root/bench-runs/h6-9b05e95f/jsonpatch-cli.mjs:128 Handle `process.stdout` `'error'`: exit quietly on EPIPE, print one plain line for any other error, with no stack trace.
- /root/bench-runs/h6-9b05e95f/jsonpatch-cli.mjs:131-132 Replace the re-throw of non-CliError errors with one plain stderr line and `process.exitCode = 1`. A crash should never reach the user as a stack trace.
- /root/bench-runs/h6-9b05e95f/jsonpatch-cli.mjs:68 Say why the close error is ignored (read-only handle, data already read), or make the empty catch explicit with a comment.
- /root/bench-runs/h6-9b05e95f/jsonpatch-cli.mjs:103,109,111 Add a helper `dataError(name, reason)` returning exit 3, alongside `readError`.
- /root/bench-runs/h6-9b05e95f/jsonpatch.mjs:147-166 Give `checkOperation` one return type, e.g. `{ reason }` or `{ op }`, and build the result in a single object instead of filling in `parsed.from`, `parsed.value` and so on.
- /root/bench-runs/h6-9b05e95f/jsonpatch.mjs:48 Use `dst.push(copy)` for arrays and keep `setMember` for objects only.
- /root/bench-runs/h6-9b05e95f/jsonpatch.mjs:178 Add a comment that comparing the raw strings is the same as comparing tokens, because the `~0`/`~1` encoding is one-to-one.
- test/cli-io.test.mjs (new case) Add tests for a deep result made by repeated `copy` and for writing to a closed stdout pipe. Each should expect one stderr line and no stack trace.

content.text:
The fix round passes your gate: overall 9/10 and no item under 7. I re-ran the tests and coverage, repeated the earlier crash probes and checked the new code.

- **Tests:** `npm test` gives 574 pass, 0 fail, 1 skip (running as root). Coverage is 100% for `jsonpatch.mjs` and 99.4% lines / 90% branches for `jsonpatch-cli.mjs`; only line 84 (the stdin read-error branch) never runs.
- **Output matches:** the new `stringify` printed the same text as `JSON.stringify(v, null, 2)` on every sample I tried. These covered mixed nesting, empty `[]` and `{}`, `__proto__`, a `"1"` member with -0, escaped keys, `\u2028`, a lone surrogate, plain strings, -0 and 1e300.
- **Deep result:** the 4-copy version of my earlier probe (16,000 levels, 512 MB of output) now prints in full and exits 0. The 5-copy version would need about 2 GB, more than V8's maximum string length, so `JSON.stringify` could not print it either. It now ends with one line, `Error: unexpected failure`, exit 1, no stack trace.
- **Closed output pipe:** piping into `head -c 10` now exits 1 with nothing on stderr.
- **Library:** `checkOperation` now returns either `{ reason }` or `{ op }`, built as one object. The form-rule order is unchanged. The `samePath` shortcut is still only taken for move/copy, and arrays are copied with `push`. Member order, -0 and `__proto__` are still correct.

Nothing blocks a pass. Two small optional cleanups are in the fix list below.

## GRADE
Overall: 9/10
Verdict: pass
structure: 9 — focused functions, nothing nested deeply, `checkOperation` now returns one consistent shape
naming: 9 — clear, spec-aligned names (`member`, `samePath`, `dataError`, `stringify`)
duplication: 9 — `readError` and `dataError` differ only in exit code, which is acceptable
size: 10 — files about 223 and 179 lines, `stringify` 31 lines, everything else smaller
errors: 9 — the deep-result and closed-pipe crashes are fixed and every failure is one line with no stack trace; the over-size case's "unexpected failure" message is vague
tests: 9 — 574 pass, coverage about 99%, new tests check exact output, a 7000-deep result and a closed pipe; stdin read-error branch (line 84) never runs
security: 10 — no secrets or injection; `__proto__` is written with defineProperty, so there is no prototype pollution
leftovers: 10 — no debug output, commented-out code or TODOs
Fixes:
- /root/bench-runs/h6-9b05e95f/jsonpatch-cli.mjs:151,167 Optional: write `parts` to stdout in chunks instead of `join('')`, so results over V8's maximum string length still print. Or catch that RangeError and say `Error: result too large`, not `unexpected failure`.
- /root/bench-runs/h6-9b05e95f/test/cli-io.test.mjs Optional: add a test where reading stdin fails (for example a closed or write-only fd 0) so `jsonpatch-cli.mjs:84` runs.
